Tractor Tannie

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Marconette started competing on a school level four years ago and then started playing SA CHAMPS.
From grade 9 began competing in the senior class and with the clubs.
SA champs 142 competitors from 18 clubs across SA

This is the story of Corne else’s crazy journey to get her daughter to the Tug-of-war world champions that will give all South Africans 10 minutes of hope and pride in our nation.

Corne’s daughter Marconette, is a South African champion tug-of-war competitor – who even knew this was a thing? But it is, and it’s enormous!
She gets invited to the World Champs in August, but there is no government funding for this sport, so her mom has to devise a plan.

She starts baking brownies, “but people can only buy so many brownies,” so that didn’t work.

Corne explains how the Afrikaans word for tug of war reminded her of the little tractor they bought 20 years ago. And so she decides to go on a crazy journey and raise the money for her daughter – 1780 km over 13 days through some of SA’s smallest towns.

To start the fundraiser, Corne created a video explaining her story and showing her route. People began offering her free accommodation, food, and support within a few days. This was nothing compared to what happened once she hit the road. “People would line up at the entrance to the town to welcome me and give me hugs.”
“People cooked for me and shared stories. It was like we became best friends overnight.”

Corne has so many stories from the road a sister gave her a letter to deliver to her family 200km away. She carried beanies for another stranger and gave them to a group of kids who came out to dance for her. She did Van Reenens pass at 8km/hour in the rain and the mist, with trucks backed up behind her for miles.

When it feels like your country is imploding, all we have is each other. This is something South Africans are good at; we are so hungry for the hope that as soon as a character like Corne and her tiny tractor comes along, we jump on that joy wagon. We want a reason to celebrate our country, and these stories do that.

Corne documented her journey on her phone and will give us that footage.
The SA Tug-of-war champs are on the 21st of July, her daughter is competing, and we can film there.
